success_patterns: Compare options clause by clause: properties such as uniqueness, invariance, regularity, stronger mixing, or validity without a stated hypothesis are separate claims, not automatic consequences of a plausible main conclusion.
Preserve the exact scope of universal and almost-everywhere claims, including the specified parameter locus and the measure used there.

For an equivalence, verify both implications. A restricted class of objects may still characterize a universal property when the ambient object belongs to that class and the property passes to subobjects.
For identities and named results, match the exact object and formula; signs, coefficients, parameter placement, and theorem hypotheses can distinguish otherwise similar options.

patch.reasoning: The existing skill already covers exact option auditing, theorem matching, and formula checks. Two useful operational details from this batch are worth making explicit: an almost-everywhere claim on a null locus must use the measure specified on that locus, and equivalences involving subobjects can follow from inheritance even when the quantified classes differ.

edits.target: distinctions such as conditioned versus unconditioned laws can change the conclusion.
edits.content: - In an “almost every” claim restricted to a locus—especially one of ambient measure zero—use the measure specified on that locus. Almost-everywhere with respect to ambient measure and with respect to a natural or conditioned measure on the locus are different claims.

edits.target: For an equivalence, check both implications.
edits.content: - When a universal property over all subobjects is compared with the same property over a restricted class, do not infer non-equivalence from the narrower quantifier alone. Check whether the ambient object belongs to the restricted class and whether the property is inherited by subobjects; together these can establish the reverse implication.
